newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska corn development eight days behind normal.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska corn development eight days behind normal.

text.p: Corn development in Nebraska as of Sunday was about eight days behind normal, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
Seventy-one percent of the crop was in the dough stage of development, up from 52 percent a year ago but behind the five-year average of 75 percent.
The corn crop was one percent very poor, two percent poor, 12 percent fair, 59 percent good and 26 percent excellent.
Ninety-five percent of the soybean crop was setting pods, up from 79 percent a year ago and above the 89 percent average pace.
Soybean conditions were two percent poor, 11 percent fair, 56 percent good and 31 percent excellent.
Sorghum condition was two percent poor, 18 percent fair, 56 percent good and 24 percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was 10 percent short, 83 percent adequate and seven percent surplus.
Pasture and range condition was five percent poor, 21 percent fair, 62 percent good and 12 percent excellent.
